grounds.point: Section 14(1)(b) requires a post-9 June 1952 subletting, assignment or other parting with possession without the landlord's written consent.
grounds.explanation: The supplied statute makes both the qualifying transfer or parting with possession and absence of written landlord consent material to the fixed ground. Section 16 separately confirms the date-sensitive treatment of subletting and the requirement of previous written consent after commencement.

grounds.point: Respondent No. 1 sublet or otherwise parted with possession of portions of the premises to Respondents No. 2 to 6.
grounds.explanation: The landlord alleged that Respondents No. 2 to 6 had exclusive possession and that Respondent No. 1 retained no portion, while Respondent No. 1 and Respondent No. 6 described the occupiers as licensees and asserted continued legal possession by the bank. The allowed record supplies these competing positions but no withheld appellate finding resolving whether the arrangements constituted subletting or parting with possession.

grounds.point: The landlord gave written consent satisfying section 14(1)(b) for the alleged subtenancies.
grounds.explanation: The prior Rent Controller is reported to have found, from the 1944 lease deed, rent receipt and related documents, that the landlord had consented to the sub-tenancy, and the respondents relied on the lease terms, the 1977 voucher and acceptance of increased rent. The appellant challenged that finding, asserting that the lease instead required previous written permission and that none was given; because the operative wording of the lease and receipt is not reproduced in the allowed record, the prior finding must be preserved but cannot be upgraded into an independently verified finding that the statutory written-consent requirement was satisfied.

grounds.point: Any relevant subletting or parting with possession to Respondents No. 2 to 6 occurred on or after 9 June 1952.
grounds.explanation: Respondents No. 2 to 4 asserted possession much before the 1961 amalgamation, while the 1977 voucher was relied upon as showing their possession by that later date, but no precise creation date for the alleged subtenancies is supplied. Because sections 14(1)(b) and 16 distinguish post-9 June 1952 arrangements from qualifying earlier subletting, the missing chronology prevents resolution of this statutory condition.

grounds.point: The amalgamations from Pratap Bank to Lakshmi Commercial Bank and then to Canara Bank independently constituted an assignment attracting section 14(1)(b).
grounds.explanation: The target record states that the original bank was amalgamated into Lakshmi Commercial Bank and later into Canara Bank, but it does not supply the governing schemes or orders establishing the precise statutory mechanism. General Radio describes section 14(b) broadly enough to reach even involuntary transfers, while Telesound gives only a prima facie view concerning amalgamation vesting and expressly reserves the section 14(1)(b) question; section 44A describes statutory vesting in a sanctioned banking-company amalgamation but does not itself establish immunity from the rent-control restriction.

reason: The supplied material does not resolve the essential statutory predicates of a qualifying post-9 June 1952 subletting, assignment or parting with possession without written landlord consent. The prior Rent Controller's consent finding is significant opposing evidence, while the factual chronology, possession character and legal effect of the bank amalgamations remain unresolved within the supplied scope, so the fixed eviction ground cannot be established or rejected conclusively.
